info.name: Game Service
info.description:
Game Service, run through the Gateway.

Run the whole collection in order: it registers a player and logs in, creates its other players and items in the Player Service, plays a session through a timed action and a night of zombies, and checks that the results reached the Player Service.

Three things to know before running it:

1. The Gateway and both services must be up. The Game Service calls the Player Service synchronously, through the Gateway, so without them a session cannot even be created.
2. The Gateway runs with AUTH_MODE=secret and the same JWT_SECRET as the Player Service, and the same INTERNAL_KEY as the Game Service.
3. Start the Game Service with DEMO_SPEEDUP=60. Actions really do take 5 to 10 minutes otherwise, and the polling requests here would sit there for all of it.

{{gatewayUrl}} takes every request, with Authorization: Bearer {{token}} set by the Log in request. {{gameUrl}} and {{playerUrl}} are the services themselves, used only for their /health, which the Gateway does not forward.

Headless:

    npx newman run postman/game-service.postman_collection.json

Usernames carry a per-run id, so it can be run repeatedly without cleaning the database.

WebSockets are not covered here beyond asking the Gateway for the URL: newman cannot hold a socket open. Use go run ./scripts/wswatch 'ws://localhost:8082/game?session_id=<id>' for that.

request.description: Polls itself with postman.setNextRequest until the action is done. Run the service with DEMO_SPEEDUP=60 or this waits ten real minutes.

exec: // Postman has no sleep and the engine ticks once a second, so wait a beat
// before polling again. With newman you can also pass --delay-request 1000.
// Poll until the engine completes it. At DEMO_SPEEDUP=60 a five minute
// scavenge takes five seconds; the cap stops this looping forever if
postman.setNextRequest("Wait for the engine to finish it");

item.description: Its own session and player, with the action started immediately. A day lasts ten seconds at DEMO_SPEEDUP=60, so a session left sitting around is already at night, where a zombie changes the very XP this asserts on.
